newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Ippa, Aegon ads misleading - consumer body.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Ippa, Aegon ads misleading - consumer body.

text.p: Financial advertisements aimed at Belgian retail investors published by Belgian bank Ippa and Dutch insurance group Aegon are misleading, Belgian consumer organisation Test Achat/Test Aankoop (TA) said on Tuesday.

TA said in a statement that Ippa is advertising bank savings certificates with a 13-percent yield, but that this is not an annualised yield, which is misleading. TA also blasted Aegon for comparing low yields on savings accounts with an investment fund in stocks and bonds.

"These two examples illustrate a trend in advertising for investment products...advertisements with 'inflated' figures say nothing about the true yield of the investement and make gullible investors believe that a yield is offered which does not correspond to reality," TA said.

"We do not share TA's opnion. We are not the only bank advertising high yields. It is just an eye-catcher. In all our sales points, the annualised yields are clearly stated," Ippa product manager Kris Willems told Reuters.
Aegon could not be reached for comment.
